newsitem.title: UK: Aston Villa has yr pretax loss due transfers.
newsitem.headline: Aston Villa has yr pretax loss due transfers.

text.p: English soccer club Aston Villa Plc, which floated on the London Stock Exchange in May, on Tuesday reported a pre-tax loss of 3.9 million stg in the year to May 31 as a result of net transfer fees of 9.3 million.
This compares with a pre-tax profit of 0.05 million stg the year before.

However, operating profit before transfer fees was 5.4 million stg, down from 6.2 million the year before, following a drop in gate receipts from knock-out cup competitions and as a result of a rise in payroll costs from securing young players to long-term contracts.
"A milestone year in the history of Aston Villa FC sees the company with profitability in excess of that forecast at the time of the flotation," chairman Doug Ellis said in a statement.

"I am confident that on the playing side we have a squad and management that will see us continuing as one of the tops sides in the Premier League and hopefully more successful in the 1997/98 Cup competitions".
Turnover in the year increased 17 percent to 22.1 million stg.
The company said that the first dividend is expected to be the interim one in respect of the six months to November 30 this year.
The club is considering proposals for increasing its stadium capacity to more than 45,000 from 39,339. The average attendance in the 1996/97 season was 36,027 versus 32,614 in the season before.
The outlook for the current year is for continued growth in all its core revenue streams, including a minimum 10 percent increase in ticket prices and growing catering and hospitality facilities.
Shares in Aston Villa were up 12-1/2 pence to 925 at 0800 GMT.
